verdict.rationale: Dagster provides asset checks to validate schema/data quality (e.g. verifying a tabular asset adheres to a specified schema) and can model dbt tests as asset checks, plus declarative automation/sensors/schedules to control when downstream assets rerun based on upstream state changes, giving engineers policy-driven propagation rather than silent breakage. However, there is no explicit evidence of automatic upstream schema-change detection (e.g. diffing schemas, alerting specifically on schema drift) as a first-class feature — the asset-check mechanism requires the engineer to author the check rather than Dagster natively detecting schema drift. Missing for 10: dedicated schema-diff/schema-drift detection feature, evidence of automatic column/type change alerts, and independent/hands-on confirmation that this workflow reliably prevents silent breakage in production.
